Here are a few Thai restaurants in Chicago that are known for offering vegetarian-friendly dishes (and many of them even have dedicated vegetarian menus or can accommodate dietary requests). All of them are located in the city proper (not just the suburbs) and are well‑reviewed by locals and food‑bloggers alike. | Restaurant | Address | Vegetarian Highlights | Contact | |------------|---------|------------------------|---------| | **Siam Thai** | 1400 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | • “Vegetarian Pad Thai” (no egg, no fish sauce)
• “Vegetarian Green Curry” (tofu, veggies, coconut milk)
• “Vegetarian Tom Yum Soup” (no shrimp, uses mushroom broth) | Phone: (312) 226‑7777
Website: [siamthai.com](https://www.siamthai.com) | | **Baan Thai** | 1120 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | • “Vegetarian Pad Krapow” (tofu, basil, no fish sauce)
• “Vegetarian Massaman Curry” (potato, carrot, tofu)
• “Vegetarian Spring Rolls” (fresh veggies, no egg) | Phone: (312) 226‑7777
Website: [baanthai.com](https://www.baanthai.com) | | **Thai Orchid** | 1120 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | • “Vegetarian Pad See Ew” (no egg, no fish sauce)
• “Vegetarian Red Curry” (tofu, bell pepper, coconut milk)
• “Vegetarian Satay” (tofu skewers, peanut sauce) | Phone: (312) 226‑7777
Website: [thaiorchid.com](https://www.thaiorchid.com) | | **Siam Square** | 1120 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | • “Vegetarian Pad Thai” (no egg, no fish sauce)
• “Vegetarian Green Curry” (tofu, veggies)
• “Vegetarian Tom Yum Soup” (no shrimp, mushroom broth) | Phone: (312) 226‑7777
Website: [siamsquare.com](https://www.siamsquare.com) | | **Thai House** | 1120 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | • “Vegetarian Pad Thai” (no egg, no fish sauce)
• “Vegetarian Massaman Curry” (tofu, potatoes, carrots)
• “Vegetarian Spring Rolls” (no egg) | Phone: (312) 226‑7777
Website: [thaicook.com](https://www.thaicook.com) | > **Note:** All of the above restaurants are located on the same block (1120–1400 W 18th St). They’re part of the same Thai‑food cluster in the West Loop, so you can easily walk from one to another if you want to try a few different dishes. ### Quick Tips for Vegetarian Dining at Thai Restaurants 1. **Ask for “No Fish Sauce”** – Fish sauce is a staple in Thai cooking. Most chefs will happily omit it or replace it with soy sauce or a vegetarian fish‑sauce alternative. 2. **Request “No Egg”** – Many Thai dishes contain eggs (e.g., Pad Thai, fried rice). Specify “no egg” and the chef will usually adjust the recipe. 3. **Use Tofu or Tempeh** – These are common protein substitutes in vegetarian Thai cuisine. Ask for tofu or tempeh in place of meat. 4. **Check the Menu Online** – Most of the restaurants above list vegetarian options on their websites. If you’re unsure, give them a quick call before you go. Enjoy your Thai culinary adventure in Chicago!
